name: packed_simd
baseline: ISPC (ispc and ispc_tasks builds of the stock ISPC example programs)
workload: Ports of the ISPC example programs (aobench 800x600, stencil, mandelbrot 800x800, options_pricing Black-Scholes and binomial put) written with packed_simd vectors plus rayon, timed against the same programs compiled with ISPC, on three x86 machines.
claimed_speedup: README summary, packed_simd+rayon vs ISPC: aobench [-1.02x, +1.53x]; stencil [+1.06x, +1.72x]; mandelbrot [-1.74x, +1.2x]; options_pricing black_scholes +1.0x, binomial_put +1.4x ('+' is speed-up, '-' slowdown). Per-example readmes: aobench tiled_par 98 ms vs ispc_tasks 150 ms on the 28-core Xeon E5-2690 v4, 102 ms vs 153 ms on the 40-core Xeon Gold 6148, 578 ms vs 567 ms on the dual-core i5; stencil vector_par 167 ms vs ispc_tasks 395 ms (E5-2690 v4); mandelbrot simd 25.1 ms vs ispc 14.4 ms on the E5-2690 v4 (1.74x slower) but 21.0 ms vs 25.7 ms on the i5. Single-thread SIMD against the crate's own scalar loop: aobench vector 4.0x, stencil vector 4.5x, mandelbrot simd 4.1x on the i5.
compiler_and_flags: rustc nightly (rust-toolchain file says only 'nightly', no pinned date); examples/*/benchmark.sh builds with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' cargo build --release --no-default-features and times with hyperfine; ISPC built through the ispc crate (build.rs targets SSE2, SSE4, AVX1, AVX2, AVX512KNL ISAs); rustc and ispc versions and ISPC flags not stated.
hardware: Dual-core AVX1 Core i5 @ 1.8 GHz (exact model not given); 28-core Xeon E5-2690 v4 @ 2.60 GHz; 40-core Xeon Gold 6148 @ 2.40 GHz
tradeoffs: Nightly-only Rust. Archived by the owner on 2026-09-16 and superseded by rust-lang/portable-simd (std::simd), so new code should use that. Vector API very close to std::simd. Optional sleef-sys dependency for transcendental functions on x86_64. The README says SPMD is not the intended use and that combining it with rayon 'poorly emulates' ISPC's model; matching ISPC needs care (performance guide).
caveats: First-party numbers from the project's own examples; README ranges mix wins and losses (aobench and mandelbrot each have a slowdown, mandelbrot on the 28-core Xeon is 1.74x slower than ISPC). Results are undated (examples date from about 2018); rustc nightly and ISPC versions are not stated and the i5 model is not given, so not fully reproducible. The headline ratios compare the rayon-parallel Rust variants with ISPC's task builds (ispc_tasks); the serial ISPC rows are slower. The baseline is ISPC, not std::arch or platform intrinsics; no direct intrinsics comparison was found. The last code change was 2023-07-30 (0.3.9); the 2026-09-15 commit is the deprecation notice. Per-example readmes were read via raw.githubusercontent.com (examples/aobench, stencil, mandelbrot, options_pricing readme.md). The book's claim about this crate was not consulted.
found_via: seed-record pass; started from https://github.com/rust-lang/packed_simd (README Performance section, example readmes)

name: Rust portable SIMD (std::simd / portable-simd)
baseline: scalar loops (Rust for-loop and Rust iterator version; also a C for-loop and NumPy as reference rows)
workload: Independent 'sp' benchmark: count transitions over 12 MiB of random ASCII 's'/'p' characters (random_sp) or random printable ASCII, with the Rust portable_simd version processing 16 bytes at a time, against scalar Rust, iterator Rust, C and NumPy versions.
claimed_speedup: random_sp: portable_simd 19.874 GiB/s (589,654 ns/iter) vs Rust iter 3.978 GiB/s, Rust for_loop 1.482 GiB/s, C for_loop 1.482 GiB/s, NumPy 5.711 GiB/s; about 5.0x over the Rust iterator and 13.4x over the Rust for-loop (derived from page data). random_printable: 19.870 vs 3.979 and 1.481 GiB/s.
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.68.0-nightly (61a415be5 2023-01-12), LLVM 15.0.6, Apple clang 14.0.0 for the C rows; run with cargo bench, optimization flags not stated explicitly (default bench profile).
hardware: Apple MacBook Pro M1 (2020), 8 GB RAM, up to 3.2 GHz, 12 MB L2
stars_or_usage: 1.1k stars; the std::simd implementation in Rust nightly
tradeoffs: Nightly-only (#![feature(portable_simd)]), API unstable. One Simd<T, N> type for every architecture, lanes up to 64, aliases up to 512-bit; masks have unspecified layout. The std::simd docs say arch-specific intrinsics may sometimes be slightly faster, with slightly different semantics, for example min without strict IEEE handling.
caveats: The measured repo is a third-party single-author demo (3 stars, AGPL-3.0 benchmark code; the library itself is Apache-2.0 OR MIT), one workload on one Apple M1 (NEON) machine with a 2023 nightly, so portable_simd of today may differ. The baselines are scalar loops in the same task; the author notes the Rust iterator version is autovectorized poorly and the C original is branchy. No comparison against std::arch intrinsics or C++ std::experimental::simd/xsimd was found; the portable-simd README has no benchmark numbers, and the book's roughly 41 percent matrix-multiply figure (first-party, author's machine) was not checked. Correctness is tested in the repo (all implementations asserted equal). A portable-simd PR #548 (AVX2 swizzle_dyn) reports 33 percent less time on a Zen 2 laptop, but against the library's own previous code and with no compiler stated.
found_via: seed-record pass; started from https://github.com/rust-lang/portable-simd; numbers found via WebSearch result https://github.com/eddieantonio/fast-sp
